svg.title: Basic Rollup: transaction lifecycle
svg.desc: One v1 SOL transfer: the client fetches a blockhash, signs a v1 transfer and posts it to /submit_transaction. The sequencer runs decode, validate, load, budget, process and commit, each with the Solana Mainnet limits it enforces and the HTTP status returned when it refuses. The result is a state change, a receipt and, planned, settlement on a cluster.
svg.text: One v1 SOL transfer from rollup_client through the sequencer's six phases, with the Solana Mainnet limits each phase enforces.
The sequencer's issue_blockhash returns a fresh
hash and keeps the last 150 it issued. A
transaction must use one of them.
A v1 transfer, signed by the payer
The frontend decodes it, sends SequencerMessage::Submit
over mpsc::channel(128) and waits on a oneshot reply.
Sequencer::execute(): one transaction at a time
Wire bytes over the limit for
feature must be active for v1
the raise to 128 is not active
reads the limits from the v1
charges the fee and runs the
fee payer cannot pay the fee
and the receipt as one step.
readers never see half of it
Preferred direction: a devnet program takes control of
the accounts while the rollup uses them, locking them on
the cluster, and moves the final lamports between them at
settlement. Until then nothing is written back or locked.
Numbers from README.md and the source. HTTP statuses from frontend.rs.
